findings.title: Materials' 50-point lens gap signals earnings cliff
findings.body: Materials trades at 17.52x forward but 38.39x trailing, a 54 percent compression that implies 119 percent earnings growth. The trailing multiple sits at the 92nd percentile while the forward multiple is near mid-range, meaning the market is pricing a dramatic normalization that has not yet shown up in reported results.

findings.title: Consumer Staples' forward price ignores trailing richness
findings.body: Consumer Staples' trailing P/E is at the 84th percentile, yet its forward multiple sits at the 36th percentile, a 48-point gap. Analysts are underwriting 44 percent earnings growth, a bold assumption for a defensive sector that typically delivers single-digit expansion.

findings.title: Energy's month-long surge hits a valuation ceiling
findings.body: Energy's forward percentile jumped 23 points in a month to 63, while its trailing percentile holds at 79. The 28 percent multiple compression implies 39 percent earnings growth, but the forward multiple is now richer than its five-year midpoint, leaving little room for further re-rating without earnings delivery.
